[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved episodes where the tape looked like this, the median 5-session forward return was 0.05%, with outcomes split exactly evenly between positive and negative results. The single number to anchor on is the 10th percentile of -4.76%, which marks the threshold below which one in ten historical analogs fell over the following week. This is a description of a historical conditional distribution, not a forecast or a recommendation to buy or sell BABA into earnings.

[state]
The engine retrieved these specific analogs because BABA's current state is defined by deep underperformance and distance from highs. The most distinctive features are its distance from the 52-week high at -41.23% (z-score -1.798), a 20-session return versus benchmark of -13.37% (z-score -1.459), and an absolute 20-session return of -13.25% (z-score -1.442). These are paired with elevated 20-session realised volatility of 42.99% (z-score 0.685) and a sharp WTI crude change over 20 days of 19.24% (z-score 1.124). The calendar days to next earnings release feature registers at 45 days (z-score 0.663), meaning the retrieval did not isolate immediate pre-earnings sessions but rather states sharing this broader technical and macro signature. Macro context from the signals block shows a VIX level of 15.44 and a 10y-2y Treasury slope of 0.25. Market sentiment sits in the Greed band with a fearGreedValue of 70. Relevant headlines framing the backdrop include CNBC Markets reporting that "Stock futures are flat as investors grapple with higher yields, await Fed minutes" and "'Unwelcome and unsafe': Why Japanese companies are retreating from China at a historic rate." Derivatives positioning data is unavailable on this card.

[history]
Across the 50 analogs, the mean 5-session return was 0.96% and the median was 0.05%, with a standard deviation of 6.64%. The distribution ranges from -20.44% to 21.43% and carries a slight positive skew of 0.321. Exactly 50% of the analogs finished above zero and 50% finished below. The bad tail is populated by severe drawdowns: 10% of episodes fell more than -4.76%, and 2% fell more than -10%. The closest match, AVGO on 2026-09-08 (distance 0.4227), returned -7.95% with a max adverse excursion of -8.32%. ADBE on 2025-07-08 returned -4.72%, META on 2026-08-13 returned -8.26%, and NKE on 2026-09-03 returned -5.08%. BABA itself appeared twice in the top matches; the session on 2026-09-08 (distance 0.4532) returned -2.95%. Conversely, NIO on 2025-07-08 returned 21.43% and INTC on 2025-08-11 returned 14.58%, illustrating the wide dispersion.

[tails]
A position can end near the median and still be un-holdable through the week. The median max adverse excursion across the 50 analogs was -2.11%, while the 10th percentile of max adverse excursion reached -5.89%. In 24% of the retrieved episodes, the path breached a 5% drawdown intra-horizon. A 10% drawdown was breached in 2% of cases, a 15% drawdown in 2%, and a 20% drawdown in 2%. The median max favourable excursion was 2.87%, yielding a reward-risk ratio of 1.36.

[stress]
The tariff-shock-2025 scenario produced the worst deterioration against the baseline: across 26 analogs, the median forward return was -3.8%, a delta of -3.85% versus the baseline median of 0.05%. The probability of falling below -10% was 30.8%, and the probability of breaching a 10% drawdown was 42.3%. Its caveat notes that policy reversals inside the window make the tail asymmetric in a way specific to that episode. The covid-crash scenario showed a median of -4.32% across 48 analogs (delta -4.37%), with a 52.1% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; its caveat states central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the rebound is baked in, making it a sample of one regime rather than a forecast. The fed-tightening-2018 scenario yielded a median of -3.26% (delta -3.31%) with a 12% breach probability, carrying the caveat that it ended with a January 2019 policy pivot that flatters late-window returns. The rate-shock-2022 scenario had a median of -3.32% (delta -3.37%) and a 14% breach probability; its caveat warns that a nine-month window means the per-date cap samples it repeatedly, so treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The carry-unwind-2024 scenario produced a median of -2.57% (delta -2.62%) with a 16.7% breach probability, caveated by the fact that the reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, making H-day returns look benign despite the intra-horizon excursion. The earnings-day shock scenario resulted in a median of -0.95% (delta -1.00%) with a 12% breach probability, caveated that earnings dates for foreign private issuers come from 6-K full-text search and are noisier than domestic 8-K dates. The liquidity-air-pocket scenario showed a median of 1.
